notes.3-4: both are a thin flake or plate on a surface; 'she scraped the scale off before cooking it' can be defended as either a crust deposit or a fish's plates

notes.0-2: 'he gave her a ring' reads as either a finger band or a phone call
notes.1-4: 'police raided the dogfighting ring' can be read as the arena where fights are held or the secret group running them
'she put the capital she gained from the merger to use' can be read as funds or as an advantage won (cf. 'political capital', 'make capital of')
